records.source: וַיְהִי֙ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה הָיָה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ בַּשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית לֵאמֹ֑ר לֵ֚ךְ הֵרָאֵ֣ה אֶל־אַחְאָ֔ב וְאֶתְּנָ֥ה מָטָ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was [after] many days, and [the] word of Yahweh came to Elijah in the year the third, saying, Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain on [the] face of the ground.
pieces: After many days, in the third year, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Elijah: "Go and appear before Ahab, and I will send rain on the land."

L.1: And it was [after] many days, and the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah in the third year, saying, "Go, show yourself to Ahab, and I will give rain on the face of the ground."

R.1: A long time passed. Then in the third year, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Elijah this message: "Go and let Ahab see you. I am going to send rain on the land again."

decisions.choice: the third year: most likely the third year of the drought
alternatives: the third year of Elijah's stay in Zarephath
decisions.reason: The drought began when Elijah announced it to Ahab (17:1). "The third year" is most naturally counted from then, or from Elijah's stay in Zarephath (17:9). Luke 4:25 and James 5:17 speak of three and a half years without rain, which fits a drought that had run into its third year or beyond.

decisions.choice: show yourself: appear in person before the king
decisions.reason: The verb means "let yourself be seen". Elijah had been hidden since he announced the drought (17:3), and Ahab had searched for him everywhere (verse 10). Now he is to come out into the open.

decisions.choice: I will give rain: the drought ends at Yahweh's word
decisions.reason: Elijah had said there would be no rain except at his word (17:1). Rain is Yahweh's gift (Deuteronomy 11:13-17), not Baal's, the god of storm and rain whom Ahab served (16:31-32). The chapter shows who truly sends it.

decisions.choice: show yourself (Literal); present yourself (Balanced); let Ahab see you (Readable); the land (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the usual word for coming before a king. Balanced and Readable say "the land" for "the face of the ground".

records.heading: Elijah and Obadiah

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֵֽלִיָּ֔הוּ לְהֵרָא֖וֹת אֶל־אַחְאָ֑ב וְהָרָעָ֖ב חָזָ֥ק בְּשֹׁמְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And went Elijah to show himself to Ahab; and the famine [was] severe in Samaria.
pieces: So Elijah went to present himself to Ahab. Now the famine was severe in Samaria.

L.2: And Elijah went to show himself to Ahab. And the famine [was] severe in Samaria.

R.2: So Elijah went to meet Ahab. By this time there was a terrible shortage of food in Samaria.

decisions.choice: the famine was severe: background to what follows
decisions.reason: The clause breaks off from the main story to describe the situation, which explains Ahab's search for grass in verses 3-6. The narrative returns to Elijah's meeting in verse 7.

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital and, by extension, the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria was the city Omri, Ahab's father, built as his capital (16:24). Here it may mean the city or the whole region it ruled.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אַחְאָ֔ב אֶל־עֹבַדְיָ֖הוּ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הַבָּ֑יִת וְעֹבַדְיָ֗הוּ הָיָ֥ה יָרֵ֛א אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And summoned Ahab Obadiah who [was] over the house; and Obadiah was fearing Yahweh greatly.
pieces: Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (Obadiah was a man who deeply revered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.3: And Ahab summoned Obadiah, who [was] over the house. And Obadiah was fearing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} greatly.

R.3: Ahab called for Obadiah, the man in charge of his palace. Obadiah had great respect for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and worshiped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: over the house: the steward who managed the king's palace and estates
decisions.reason: This was a high office at court (4:6; 16:9; 2 Kings 18:18; Isaiah 22:15). Ahab trusts Obadiah with the search for fodder for the royal animals (verse 5).

decisions.choice: feared Yahweh greatly: was devoted to Yahweh
decisions.reason: To fear Yahweh is to honor him as God and live in obedience to him (Proverbs 1:7; Deuteronomy 10:12). Obadiah's name means "servant of Yahweh", and in Ahab's court, where Baal was served (16:31-32), his loyalty was dangerous.

decisions.choice: the parenthesis opened here closes at the end of verse 4
decisions.reason: Balanced marks the note about Obadiah's past (verses 3b-4) as an aside, because the story of Ahab's order resumes in verse 5.

decisions.choice: had great respect for the LORD and worshiped him
decisions.reason: Readable explains "fearing" so that it is not taken as being afraid.

records.source: וַיְהִי֙ בְּהַכְרִ֣ית אִיזֶ֔בֶל אֵ֖ת נְבִיאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקַּ֨ח עֹבַדְיָ֜הוּ מֵאָ֣ה נְבִאִ֗ים וַֽיַּחְבִּיאֵ֞ם חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וְכִלְכְּלָ֖ם לֶ֥חֶם וָמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it was when cut off Jezebel the prophets of Yahweh, and took Obadiah a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty man in a cave, and supplied them [with] bread and water.
pieces: When Jezebel was killing off the prophets of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, Obadiah had taken a hundred of them and hidden them in caves, fifty in each, and had kept them supplied with food and water.)

L.4: And it was, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that Obadiah took a hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men to a cave, and supplied them [with] bread and water.

R.4: When Queen Jezebel was killing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s prophets, Obadiah had taken a hundred of them and hidden them in two caves, fifty in each. He had kept them supplied with food and water.

decisions.choice: cut off: killed, wiped out
decisions.reason: The verb "cut off" is used for destroying people completely (Joshua 23:4). Verse 13 says plainly that Jezebel killed the prophets of Yahweh.

decisions.choice: Jezebel: Ahab's wife, daughter of the king of Sidon
decisions.reason: Ahab married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and began to serve Baal (16:31). Her persecution of Yahweh's prophets is not told elsewhere; it is known only from this chapter and from 19:10.

decisions.choice: fifty men in a cave: fifty in each of two caves
alternatives: fifty men in one cave (a copying slip for "fifty, fifty")
decisions.reason: Read with verse 13, "fifty, fifty men in a cave", the words mean that the hundred were split into two groups of fifty, each hidden in its own cave.

decisions.choice: bread and water: food and drink
decisions.reason: "Bread" often means food in general. In a time of famine (verse 2), feeding a hundred men in secret was costly as well as dangerous.

decisions.choice: Queen Jezebel; two caves, fifty in each
decisions.reason: Readable says who Jezebel was and spells out the two caves.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ אֶל־עֹ֣בַדְיָ֔הוּ לֵ֤ךְ בָּאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶל־כָּל־מַעְיְנֵ֣י הַמַּ֔יִם וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־הַנְּחָלִ֑ים אוּלַ֣י׀נִמְצָ֣א חָצִ֗יר וּנְחַיֶּה֙ ס֣וּס וָפֶ֔רֶד וְל֥וֹא נַכְרִ֖ית מֵהַבְּהֵמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Ahab to Obadiah, Go through the land to all [the] springs of the water and to all the wadis; perhaps we will find grass and keep alive horse and mule, and not cut off from the livestock.
pieces: Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to every spring and every stream bed. Perhaps we can find grass and keep the horses and mules alive, and not have to destroy any of our animals."

L.5: And Ahab said to Obadiah, "Go through the land to all the springs of water and to all the wadis. Perhaps we will find grass and keep alive horse and mule, and we will not cut off [any] of the livestock."

R.5: Ahab told Obadiah, "Go all through the land. Look at every spring of water and every valley where a stream runs. Maybe we can find some grass so we can keep our horses and mules alive. Then we will not have to kill any of our animals."

decisions.choice: wadis: stream beds that hold water in the rainy season
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley with a stream that may run dry in summer. In the drought, the last green grass would be near springs and in the beds of such streams.

decisions.choice: horses and mules: the king's chariot and riding animals
decisions.reason: Ahab had a large chariot force (22:34; compare 10:26). Losing the horses would weaken the kingdom's army. The singular words are used for the whole kind of animal.

decisions.choice: not cut off any of the livestock: not have to lose or slaughter any animals
alternatives: not lose any animals to the famine
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Jezebel's killing of the prophets in verse 4. The king is anxious to cut off none of his animals while his queen cuts off Yahweh's prophets.

decisions.choice: stream bed (Balanced); valley where a stream runs (Readable); our animals
decisions.reason: "Wadi" is not a common English word, so Balanced and Readable describe it.

records.source: וַֽיְחַלְּק֥וּ לָהֶ֛ם אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ לַֽעֲבָר־בָּ֑הּ אַחְאָ֞ב הָלַ֨ךְ בְּדֶ֤רֶךְ אֶחָד֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְעֹֽבַדְיָ֛הוּ הָלַ֥ךְ בְּדֶרֶךְ־אֶחָ֖ד לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they divided to themselves the land to pass through it; Ahab went in way one by himself, and Obadiah went in way one by himself.
pieces: So they divided the land between them to cover it, Ahab going one way on his own and Obadiah another way on his own.

L.6: And they divided the land between them to pass through it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.

R.6: So they split up the land to search all of it. Ahab went one way alone, and Obadiah went the other way alone.

decisions.choice: Ahab went ... Obadiah went: the king himself searches
decisions.reason: The word order puts the two men side by side. That the king goes out himself shows how desperate the famine had become.

decisions.choice: another way
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "one way ... one way"; English says "one way ... another way".

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י עֹבַדְיָ֨הוּ֙ בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵלִיָּ֖הוּ לִקְרָאת֑וֹ וַיַּכִּרֵ֨הוּ֙ וַיִּפֹּ֣ל עַל־פָּנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה אֲדֹנִ֥י אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And was Obadiah on the way, and there! Elijah to meet him; and he recognized him and fell on his face and said, [Is] this you, my lord Elijah?
pieces: As Obadiah was on his way, there was Elijah coming to meet him. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down with his face to the ground, and said, "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?"

L.7: And Obadiah was on the way, and look, Elijah [was coming] to meet him. And he recognized him and fell on his face and said, "[Is] it you, my lord Elijah?"

R.7: While Obadiah was on the road, suddenly Elijah was there, coming toward him. Obadiah knew who he was. He bowed down low with his face to the ground and said, "Is that you, my master Elijah?"

decisions.choice: there!: a sudden, unexpected sight
decisions.reason: The word points to something seen at that moment, often with surprise.

decisions.choice: fell on his face: bowed to the ground in deep respect
decisions.reason: Obadiah, the king's high official, bows before the prophet as before a superior and calls him "my lord".

decisions.choice: is it you?: surprise rather than doubt
decisions.reason: Obadiah recognized Elijah, so the question expresses astonishment at finding the man the king had searched for (verse 10).

decisions.choice: look (Literal); there was (Balanced); suddenly (Readable); my master (Readable)
decisions.reason: English has no single word for the Hebrew pointing word. Readable uses "master" so that "lord" is not read as a title for God.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר ל֖וֹ אָ֑נִי לֵ֛ךְ אֱמֹ֥ר לַאדֹנֶ֖יךָ הִנֵּ֥ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said to him, I; go, say to your lord, Here [is] Elijah.
pieces: He answered him, "It is. Go and tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"

L.8: And he said to him, "I [am]. Go, say to your lord, 'Here [is] Elijah.'"

R.8: Elijah said, "Yes, it is me. Go and tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"

decisions.choice: your lord: Ahab
decisions.reason: Obadiah has called Elijah "my lord" (verse 7); Elijah points him back to the master he actually serves, the king. The form is plural, a plural of majesty often used for a master.

decisions.choice: your master (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "master" here and in verses 10-14, so the reader can tell Obadiah's master Ahab from Yahweh.

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מֶ֣ה חָטָ֑אתִי כִּֽי־אַתָּ֞ה נֹתֵ֧ן אֶֽת־עַבְדְּךָ֛ בְּיַד־אַחְאָ֖ב לַהֲמִיתֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: And he said, What have I sinned, that you [are] giving your servant into [the] hand of Ahab to put me to death?
pieces: Obadiah said, "What sin have I committed, that you are handing your servant over to Ahab to be put to death?

L.9: And he said, "What have I sinned, that you [are] giving your servant into the hand of Ahab to put me to death?

R.9: But Obadiah said, "What wrong have I done? Why are you handing your servant over to Ahab? He will kill me!

decisions.choice: your servant: Obadiah's polite way of speaking of himself
decisions.reason: Speaking of oneself as "your servant" was a courteous form of address to a superior (Genesis 18:3; 1 Samuel 20:7-8).

decisions.choice: what have I sinned: what wrong have I done to deserve this
decisions.reason: Obadiah does not confess a sin. He protests that he has done nothing to deserve being sent to his death.

decisions.choice: your servant at every level
decisions.reason: Polite self-reference keeps "your servant" at every level, as Genesis 18:3 and 1 Samuel 20 do. Obadiah's speech runs to verse 14, so this record leaves the quotation open.

records.source: חַ֣י׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אִם־יֶשׁ־גּ֤וֹי וּמַמְלָכָה֙ אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־שָׁלַ֨ח אֲדֹנִ֥י שָׁם֙ לְבַקֶּשְׁךָ֔ וְאָמְר֖וּ אָ֑יִן וְהִשְׁבִּ֤יעַ אֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָה֙ וְאֶת־הַגּ֔וֹי כִּ֖י לֹ֥א יִמְצָאֶֽכָּה׃
records.gloss: [As] lives Yahweh your God, if there is a nation and kingdom where not has sent my lord there to seek you; and they said, [He is] not [here], and he made swear the kingdom and the nation that not it has found you.
pieces: As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God lives, my master has sent people to look for you in every nation and kingdom. Whenever a nation said, 'He is not here,' he made its people swear that they could not find you.

L.10: [As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you. And when they said, '[He is] not [here],' he made the kingdom and the nation swear that they had not found you.

R.10: I promise you, as surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God lives, my master has sent men to every nation and kingdom to look for you. When the people of a nation said, 'He is not here,' Ahab made them swear an oath that they really could not find you.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives: an oath
decisions.reason: The words call on the living God as witness that what follows is true (Judges 8:19; 1 Samuel 14:39).

decisions.choice: if there is a nation: there is no nation
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if there is" means "there is not": the speaker leaves unsaid the curse he would accept if it were so.

decisions.choice: made them swear: Ahab demanded an oath
decisions.reason: Ahab did not trust a simple denial. He made the rulers of each land swear that Elijah was not hiding there. The search shows that Ahab held Elijah responsible for the drought (verse 17).

decisions.choice: there is no nation (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal gives the meaning of the oath form, since "if there is" would mislead in English.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֖ה אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֑ר לֵ֛ךְ אֱמֹ֥ר לַאדֹנֶ֖יךָ הִנֵּ֥ה אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And now you [are] saying, Go, say to your lord, Here [is] Elijah.
pieces: And now you are telling me, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here."'

L.11: And now you [are] saying, 'Go, say to your lord, "Here [is] Elijah."'

R.11: And now you tell me, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here!"'

decisions.choice: and now: the contrast with Ahab's long search
decisions.reason: Obadiah repeats Elijah's words to show how impossible the order seems after all the king's searching.

decisions.choice: quotations inside quotations
decisions.reason: Obadiah quotes Elijah, who quotes what Obadiah is to say, so the words take single and then double quotation marks.

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה אֲנִ֣י׀אֵלֵ֣ךְ מֵאִתָּ֗ךְ וְר֨וּחַ יְהוָ֤ה׀יִֽשָּׂאֲךָ֙ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־אֵדָ֔ע וּבָ֨אתִי לְהַגִּ֧יד לְאַחְאָ֛ב וְלֹ֥א יִֽמְצָאֲךָ֖ וַהֲרָגָ֑נִי וְעַבְדְּךָ֛ יָרֵ֥א אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה מִנְּעֻרָֽי׃
records.gloss: And it will be, I will go from you, and [the] Spirit of Yahweh will carry you to where not I know; and I will come to tell Ahab and not he will find you, and he will kill me; and your servant has feared Yahweh from my youth.
pieces: As soon as I leave you, the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will carry you off to some place I do not know. Then when I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find you, he will kill me. Yet I, your servant, have revered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} since I was young.

L.12: And it will be, [when] I go from you, that the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will carry you to [a place] I do not know. And [when] I come to tell Ahab and he does not find you, he will kill me. And your servant has feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} from my youth.

R.12: As soon as I leave you, the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may carry you away to some place I do not know about. Then when I tell Ahab you are here and he cannot find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have worshiped {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} since I was a boy.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Yahweh: God's Spirit, who could move the prophet suddenly
decisions.reason: The word can mean "wind" or "spirit". Here it is Yahweh's Spirit, thought able to carry a prophet from place to place (2 Kings 2:16; Ezekiel 3:14). Obadiah fears Elijah will vanish as suddenly as he has appeared.

decisions.choice: it will be ... I go: a chain of things Obadiah expects to happen
decisions.reason: The verbs describe what Obadiah fears will follow, one after another: he leaves, Elijah is carried away, he reports, Ahab finds no one, and Ahab kills him.

decisions.choice: your servant has feared Yahweh from my youth
decisions.reason: Obadiah reminds Elijah that he is a faithful worshiper of Yahweh, as the narrator said (verse 3), and should not be thrown away. The pronoun shifts from "your servant" to "my", as often in polite speech.

decisions.choice: may carry you away (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable softens "will" to "may" because Obadiah is describing what he fears, not what he knows.

records.source: הֲלֹֽא־הֻגַּ֤ד לַֽאדֹנִי֙ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֔יתִי בַּהֲרֹ֣ג אִיזֶ֔בֶל אֵ֖ת נְבִיאֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וָאַחְבִּא֩ מִנְּבִיאֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה מֵ֣אָה אִ֗ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֨ים חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וָאֲכַלְכְּלֵ֖ם לֶ֥חֶם וָמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: Has not it been told to my lord what I did when killed Jezebel the prophets of Yahweh, and I hid of [the] prophets of Yahweh a hundred man, fifty fifty man in a cave, and supplied them [with] bread and water?
pieces: Has my lord not been told what I did when Jezebel was killing the prophets of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? I hid a hundred of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s prophets, fifty in each of two caves, and kept them supplied with food and water.

L.13: Has it not been told to my lord what I did when Jezebel killed the prophets of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I hid a hundred men of the prophets of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, fifty [and] fifty men in a cave, and supplied them [with] bread and water?

R.13: Sir, has no one told you what I did when Jezebel was killing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s prophets? I hid a hundred of them in two caves, fifty in each cave. And I gave them food and water.

decisions.choice: has it not been told: surely you have heard
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. Obadiah appeals to a deed that the prophets themselves would have reported.

decisions.choice: fifty, fifty men: fifty in each cave
decisions.reason: Repeating a number gives it a sense of "each". The hundred were split into two groups of fifty. See verse 4.

decisions.choice: my lord (Literal, Balanced); sir (Readable)
decisions.reason: Obadiah addresses Elijah politely in the third person. Readable turns it into direct address.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ אַתָּ֣ה אֹמֵ֔ר לֵ֛ךְ אֱמֹ֥ר לַֽאדֹנֶ֖יךָ הִנֵּ֣ה אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַהֲרָגָֽנִי׃ס
records.gloss: And now you [are] saying, Go, say to your lord, Here [is] Elijah; and he will kill me.
pieces: And now you are telling me, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here."' He will kill me!"

L.14: And now you [are] saying, 'Go, say to your lord, "Here [is] Elijah,"' and he will kill me!"

R.14: And now you tell me to go and tell my master that you are here! He will kill me!"

decisions.choice: and he will kill me: the end Obadiah sees ahead
decisions.reason: Obadiah repeats verse 11 word for word and adds the conclusion he has argued in verse 12. The repetition shows his fear.

decisions.choice: to go and tell my master that you are here (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the quotation within a quotation into reported speech.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵֽלִיָּ֔הוּ חַ֚י יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָמַ֖דְתִּי לְפָנָ֑יו כִּ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם אֵרָאֶ֥ה אֵלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah, [As] lives Yahweh of hosts before whom I stand, surely today I will show myself to him.
pieces: Elijah said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies lives, whom I serve, I will present myself to Ahab today."

L.15: And Elijah said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely today I will show myself to him."

R.15: Elijah said, "I serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. As surely as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, I will meet Ahab face to face today."

decisions.choice: Yahweh of hosts: Yahweh, ruler of the armies of heaven and earth
decisions.reason: "Hosts" means armies. The title presents Yahweh as commander of all the powers in heaven and on earth (1 Samuel 17:45; Psalm 24:10). Elijah uses it before he faces the king and his prophets.

decisions.choice: before whom I stand: whom I serve
decisions.reason: To stand before a king is to be in his service, ready to act on his word (10:8; 12:8). Elijah used the same words when he announced the drought (17:1).

decisions.choice: surely: the oath's promise
decisions.reason: After an oath, this word introduces what the speaker swears he will do.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (Literal); the LORD of Armies (Balanced, Readable); whom I serve
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this title in these books. Balanced and Readable say what "stand before" means.

records.heading: Elijah and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel

records.source: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ עֹבַדְיָ֛הוּ לִקְרַ֥את אַחְאָ֖ב וַיַּגֶּד־ל֑וֹ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחְאָ֖ב לִקְרַ֥את אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And went Obadiah to meet Ahab and told him; and went Ahab to meet Elijah.
pieces: So Obadiah went off to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab set out to meet Elijah.

L.16: And Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.

R.16: So Obadiah went and found Ahab and told him the news. Then Ahab went out to meet Elijah.

decisions.choice: Obadiah went ... Ahab went: the meeting is set up
decisions.reason: Two matching clauses show Obadiah obeying and the king coming. Elijah, who had hidden from Ahab (17:3), now waits for the king to come to him.

records.source: וַיְהִ֛י כִּרְא֥וֹת אַחְאָ֖ב אֶת־אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ אֵלָ֔יו הַאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה עֹכֵ֥ר יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it was as saw Ahab Elijah, and said Ahab to him, [Is] this you, troubler of Israel?
pieces: When Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, "Is it you, you troubler of Israel?"

L.17: And it was, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said to him, "[Is] it you, troubler of Israel?"

R.17: As soon as Ahab saw Elijah, he said to him, "So it is you, the man who brings trouble on Israel!"

decisions.choice: troubler of Israel: one who brings disaster on the whole people
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring ruin or disaster on a community. It is the word Joshua used to Achan, whose sin brought defeat on Israel: "Why have you troubled us? Yahweh will trouble you today" (Joshua 7:25). Ahab blames the drought on Elijah as if he were another Achan.

decisions.choice: is it you?: an accusation, not a question
decisions.reason: Obadiah used the same words in respect (verse 7: "Is it you, my lord Elijah?"). In Ahab's mouth they are a charge. The contrast shows the two men's attitudes to the prophet.

decisions.choice: troubler (Literal, Balanced); the man who brings trouble on (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Troubler" is rare in English; Readable says what it means.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לֹ֤א עָכַ֨רְתִּי֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י אִם־אַתָּ֖ה וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ בַּֽעֲזָבְכֶם֙ אֶת־מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַבְּעָלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he said, Not have I troubled Israel, but rather you and [the] house of your father, in your forsaking [the] commandments of Yahweh, and you have walked after the Baals.
pieces: Elijah answered, "I have not brought trouble on Israel. You have, you and your father's house, because you have abandoned {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s commandments and followed the Baals.

L.18: And he said, "I have not troubled Israel, but you and the house of your father [have], in your forsaking the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and you have walked after the Baals.

R.18: Elijah answered, "I am not the one who has brought trouble on Israel. You and your father's family have done that. You have turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s commands and have worshiped the Baals instead.

decisions.choice: the troubler is Ahab: disobedience brought the drought
decisions.reason: Elijah turns the charge back on the king. The law warned that if Israel turned to other gods, Yahweh would shut the sky and there would be no rain (Deuteronomy 11:16-17). The drought is the result of Ahab's sin, not of Elijah's word.

decisions.choice: your father's house: the dynasty of Omri
decisions.reason: Ahab's father Omri did evil, more than all before him (16:25-26), and Ahab went further still (16:30-33).

decisions.choice: the Baals: Baal in his many local forms and images
decisions.reason: The plural is used for Baal as worshiped at many shrines and under many local titles (Judges 2:11; 1 Samuel 7:4). To walk after them is to worship and serve them.

decisions.choice: you have forsaken (plural) ... you have walked (singular)
decisions.reason: "Your forsaking" speaks to Ahab and his family together; "you have walked" turns back to Ahab himself.

decisions.choice: commandments (Literal, Balanced); commands (Readable); followed (Balanced); worshiped (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books. Balanced and Readable say what "walk after" means. Elijah's speech goes on into verse 19.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה שְׁלַ֨ח קְבֹ֥ץ אֵלַ֛י אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶל־הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וְאֶת־נְבִיאֵ֨י הַבַּ֜עַל אַרְבַּ֧ע מֵא֣וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֗ים וּנְבִיאֵ֤י הָֽאֲשֵׁרָה֙ אַרְבַּ֣ע מֵא֔וֹת אֹכְלֵ֖י שֻׁלְחַ֥ן אִיזָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: And now send, gather to me all Israel to Mount the Carmel, and the prophets of the Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the Asherah four hundred, eaters of [the] table of Jezebel.
pieces: Now send word and gather all Israel to me at Mount Carmel, together with the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of Asherah who eat at Jezebel's table."

L.19: And now send, gather to me all Israel at Mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal, 450, and the prophets of Asherah, 400, who eat at the table of Jezebel."

R.19: Now send messengers and bring all the people of Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Bring the 450 prophets of Baal too, and the 400 prophets of the goddess Asherah, the ones Jezebel feeds at her own table."

decisions.choice: Mount Carmel: the ridge running to the sea in the northwest
decisions.reason: Carmel is a long, high ridge that ends at the Mediterranean, on the border between Israel and the Phoenician lands of Jezebel's father (16:31). It was green and fertile and had altars of its own (verse 30).

decisions.choice: Asherah: a Canaanite goddess
decisions.reason: Here Asherah is the goddess herself, not the wooden pole that stood for her (16:33). She was worshiped alongside Baal. Her prophets are not mentioned again in the chapter; only the prophets of Baal take part in the contest (verses 22, 25, 40).

decisions.choice: who eat at Jezebel's table: kept at the queen's expense
decisions.reason: To eat at a ruler's table was to be supported from the royal household (2 Samuel 9:7; 1 Kings 2:7). These prophets were Jezebel's own, paid by the court, while Yahweh's prophets hid in caves (verse 4).

decisions.choice: the goddess Asherah; send messengers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says that Asherah was a goddess, so she is not taken for a person.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אַחְאָ֖ב בְּכָל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּקְבֹּ֥ץ אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים אֶל־הַ֥ר הַכַּרְמֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And sent Ahab among all [the] sons of Israel and gathered the prophets to Mount the Carmel.
pieces: So Ahab sent word to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and gathered the prophets together at Mount Carmel.

L.20: And Ahab sent among all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and gathered the prophets at Mount Carmel.

R.20: So Ahab sent messages to all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. He brought the prophets together on Mount Carmel.

decisions.choice: Ahab sent ... and gathered: the king obeys the prophet
decisions.reason: Ahab does exactly what Elijah told him (verse 19), without a word. The king who called Elijah a troubler now carries out his orders.

decisions.choice: the prophets: the prophets of Baal
decisions.reason: The prophets gathered are those Elijah named, the prophets of Baal (and of Asherah). The people of Israel are summoned too (verse 21).

records.source: וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֗ם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ עַד־מָתַ֞י אַתֶּ֣ם פֹּסְחִים֮ עַל־שְׁתֵּ֣י הַסְּעִפִּים֒ אִם־יְהוָ֤ה הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרָ֔יו וְאִם־הַבַּ֖עַל לְכ֣וּ אַחֲרָ֑יו וְלֹֽא־עָנ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם אֹת֖וֹ דָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And came near Elijah to all the people and said, Until when [are] you limping on [the] two the branches? If Yahweh [is] the God, walk after him; and if the Baal, walk after him. And not answered the people him a word.
pieces: Elijah stepped up before all the people and said, "How long will you go on hobbling between two choices? If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is God, follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. If it is Baal, follow Baal." But the people said nothing in reply.

L.21: And Elijah came near to all the people and said, "How long [are] you limping on the two branches? If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] God, walk after {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and if Baal, walk after him." And the people did not answer him a word.

R.21: Elijah came up to all the people and said, "How long are you going to keep switching back and forth between two sides? If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the true God, follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! But if Baal is God, then follow Baal!" But the people did not say a word.

decisions.choice: limping on the two branches: wavering, unable to commit to either side
decisions.reason: The verb means to limp or hobble. The noun is rare; it is related to words for branches or divided boughs, and to a word for divided thoughts (Psalm 119:113). The picture may be of a man limping because he walks on two different crutches, of a bird hopping from branch to branch, or simply of someone who cannot choose between two opinions. Every reading gives the same point: Israel cannot keep a foot in both camps.

decisions.choice: God: the true God, the one who is really God
decisions.reason: The word has the article, "the God". The question is not whether Yahweh or Baal is a god but which of them is God in truth. The same words return in the people's cry in verse 39.

decisions.choice: walk after him: follow and worship him
decisions.reason: To walk after a god is to be his loyal follower (Deuteronomy 13:5; verse 18).

decisions.choice: limping: echoed in verse 26
decisions.reason: The same verb describes the prophets of Baal hobbling around their altar (verse 26). Israel's wavering is like their limping dance.

decisions.choice: limping on the two branches (Literal); hobbling between two choices (Balanced); switching back and forth between two sides (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture. Balanced keeps the limping and gives the sense of the rare noun. Readable says plainly what the saying means.

decisions.choice: the true God; Baal is God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the contrast and repeats the name Baal to make clear who is followed.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־הָעָ֔ם אֲנִ֞י נוֹתַ֧רְתִּי נָבִ֛יא לַיהוָ֖ה לְבַדִּ֑י וּנְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֔עַל אַרְבַּע־מֵא֥וֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁ֖ים אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah to the people, I, I am left a prophet of Yahweh, I by myself, and [the] prophets of the Baal [are] four hundred and fifty man.
pieces: Then Elijah said to the people, "I am the only one left of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s prophets, but Baal has 450 prophets.

L.22: And Elijah said to the people, "I, I am left a prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, I alone, and the prophets of Baal [are] 450 men.

R.22: Then Elijah told the people, "I am the only prophet of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who is left. But Baal has 450 prophets.

decisions.choice: I alone am left: the only prophet of Yahweh standing here
decisions.reason: Obadiah had hidden a hundred prophets of Yahweh (verses 4, 13), so Elijah means that he alone stands openly for Yahweh against the many. He says the same later in despair (19:10, 14).

decisions.choice: I am the only one left (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The repeated "I" stresses that Elijah stands alone. Balanced and Readable carry the stress by "the only". Elijah's words run on to verse 24.

records.source: וְיִתְּנוּ־לָ֜נוּ שְׁנַ֣יִם פָּרִ֗ים וְיִבְחֲר֣וּ לָהֶם֩ הַפָּ֨ר הָאֶחָ֜ד וִֽינַתְּחֻ֗הוּ וְיָשִׂ֨ימוּ֙ עַל־הָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ימוּ וַאֲנִ֞י אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה׀אֶת־הַפָּ֣ר הָאֶחָ֗ד וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ עַל־הָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א אָשִֽׂים׃
records.gloss: And let them give to us two bulls, and let them choose for themselves the bull the one and cut it in pieces and put [it] on the wood, and fire not they shall put; and I, I will prepare the bull the one and give [it] on the wood, and fire not I will put.
pieces: Have two bulls brought to us. Let the prophets of Baal pick one of the bulls for themselves, cut it up, and set it on the wood, without lighting a fire. I will get the other bull ready and set it on the wood, and I too will light no fire.

L.23: And let them give us two bulls, and let them choose the one bull for themselves and cut it in pieces and put [it] on the wood, but they shall not put fire [to it]. And I will prepare the other bull and lay [it] on the wood, but I will not put fire [to it].

R.23: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets may choose one of them. They must cut it into pieces and put it on the wood, but they must not light the fire. I will get the other bull ready and put it on the wood. I will not light a fire either.

decisions.choice: let them give ... let them choose: the first "they" is anyone, the second is Baal's prophets
decisions.reason: The first verb is impersonal: "let two bulls be given". The ones who choose are the prophets of Baal, as verse 25 makes clear.

decisions.choice: bulls cut in pieces: prepared as burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The bull was cut up and laid on the wood as for a burnt offering (Leviticus 1:6-8). The only thing missing is the fire, which each god must send.

decisions.choice: no fire: the test is which god sends fire
decisions.reason: Fire from Yahweh had consumed the first offerings at the tabernacle (Leviticus 9:24). Baal was worshiped as a storm god who sent lightning. The test is set where Baal was thought strongest.

decisions.choice: the prophets of Baal (Balanced); Baal's prophets (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" are.

records.source: וּקְרָאתֶ֞ם בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶקְרָ֣א בְשֵׁם־יְהוָ֔ה וְהָיָ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲנֶ֥ה בָאֵ֖שׁ ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיַּ֧עַן כָּל־הָעָ֛ם וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָֽר׃
records.gloss: And you will call on [the] name of your god, and I, I will call on [the] name of Yahweh; and it will be, the god who answers by fire, he [is] the God. And answered all the people and said, Good [is] the word.
pieces: Then you call on your god by name, and I will call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Whichever god answers with fire, he is God." All the people answered, "That is well said."

L.24: And you will call on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and it will be, the god who answers by fire, he [is] God." And all the people answered and said, "The word [is] good."

R.24: Then you pray to your god, and I will pray to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. The god who answers by sending fire is the real God." All the people said, "That is a good idea!"

decisions.choice: call on the name: pray to, invoke
decisions.reason: To call on a god's name is to pray to him and ask for his help (Genesis 12:8; Psalm 116:4).

decisions.choice: the god who answers by fire is God: the test of who is truly God
decisions.reason: The first "god" is general, whichever god answers; the second has the article, "the God", the true God (verse 21). The fire will settle the question.

decisions.choice: you: the prophets of Baal and those who follow Baal
decisions.reason: "Your god" is plural: it means Baal's side, whose prophets will act for them (verse 25).

decisions.choice: the word is good: the people agree
decisions.reason: The phrase accepts a proposal (Deuteronomy 1:14; 1 Kings 2:38). The people who would not answer Elijah (verse 21) now agree to the test.

decisions.choice: he: not marked as a pronoun for God
decisions.reason: The god who answers is not yet named; the pronoun refers to whichever god it will be, so it takes no capital in any setting.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ לִנְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל בַּחֲר֨וּ לָכֶ֜ם הַפָּ֤ר הָֽאֶחָד֙ וַעֲשׂ֣וּ רִאשֹׁנָ֔ה כִּ֥י אַתֶּ֖ם הָרַבִּ֑ים וְקִרְאוּ֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֔ם וְאֵ֖שׁ לֹ֥א תָשִֽׂימוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah to [the] prophets of the Baal, Choose for yourselves the bull the one and prepare [it] first, for you [are] the many; and call on [the] name of your god, and fire not you shall put.
pieces: Then Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose one of the bulls for yourselves and prepare it first, since there are many of you. Call on your god by name, but light no fire."

L.25: And Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "Choose for yourselves the one bull and prepare [it] first, for you [are] the many; and call on the name of your god, but you shall not put fire [to it]."

R.25: Elijah said to the prophets of Baal, "You go first, because there are so many of you. Choose one of the bulls and get it ready. Then pray to your god. But do not light the fire."

decisions.choice: first, for you are the many: Elijah gives them every advantage
decisions.reason: Elijah lets the many prophets of Baal go first and choose their bull. If they fail, no one can say they were treated unfairly.

decisions.choice: You go first, because there are so many of you. (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the reason at the start, since it explains the whole instruction.

records.source: וַ֠יִּקְחוּ אֶת־הַפָּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֣ן לָהֶם֮ וַֽיַּעֲשׂוּ֒ וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ בְשֵׁם־הַ֠בַּעַל מֵהַבֹּ֨קֶר וְעַד־הַצָּהֳרַ֤יִם לֵאמֹר֙ הַבַּ֣עַל עֲנֵ֔נוּ וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין עֹנֶ֑ה וַֽיְפַסְּח֔וּ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And they took the bull which he gave to them and prepared [it], and called on [the] name of the Baal from the morning and until the noon, saying, O Baal, answer us! And there [was] no voice and no one answering. And they limped about the altar which he had made.
pieces: So they took the bull that was given to them and prepared it. Then they called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, crying, "Baal, answer us!" But no sound came, and no one answered. And they kept hobbling in a dance around the altar they had made.

L.26: And they took the bull that was given to them and prepared [it], and called on the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, "O Baal, answer us!" But [there was] no voice and no one answering. And they limped about the altar that had been made.

R.26: So they took the bull they were given and got it ready. Then they prayed to Baal from morning until noon. They shouted, "Baal, answer us!" But no sound came, and no one answered. They kept dancing around the altar they had built, hopping and limping.

decisions.choice: he gave ... he had made: impersonal, "was given", "had been made"
alternatives: which he (Ahab) had given; which he had made
decisions.reason: Both verbs are singular with no subject named, a way of saying "someone". The altar is the one Baal's prophets had built. Some ancient translations read "they had made".

decisions.choice: limped about the altar: a hobbling ritual dance
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Elijah used of the people "limping" between two choices (verse 21). Here it describes a limping, bending dance around the altar, probably part of their worship. The repeated word joins the wavering people to the frantic prophets.

decisions.choice: no voice and no one answering: no response at all
decisions.reason: The same words return, with more, in verse 29. They answer the people's cry, "answer us!" with silence.

decisions.choice: limped (Literal); kept hobbling in a dance (Balanced); dancing ... hopping and limping (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the link with verse 21; Readable describes the ritual.

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י בַֽצָּהֳרַ֜יִם וַיְהַתֵּ֧ל בָּהֶ֣ם אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ קִרְא֤וּ בְקוֹל־גָּדוֹל֙ כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֣ים ה֔וּא כִּ֣י שִׂ֧יחַ וְכִֽי־שִׂ֛יג ל֖וֹ וְכִֽי־דֶ֣רֶךְ ל֑וֹ אוּלַ֛י יָשֵׁ֥ן ה֖וּא וְיִקָֽץ׃
records.gloss: And it was at noon, and mocked them Elijah and said, Call with a voice great, for a god [is] he! For musing [is he], or a going aside [is] to him, or a journey [is] to him; perhaps asleep he [is] and will wake.
pieces: At noon Elijah began to mock them. "Call out at the top of your voices!" he said. "He is a god, is he not? Maybe he is lost in thought, or he has stepped aside, or he has gone off on a trip. Or maybe he has fallen asleep, and must be woken up!"

L.27: And it was at noon, that Elijah mocked them and said, "Call with a great voice, for he [is] a god! For [he is] musing, or [he has] a going aside, or a journey [is] his; perhaps he [is] asleep and will wake up."

R.27: At noon Elijah started making fun of them. "Yell louder!" he said. "After all, he is a god! Maybe he is busy thinking. Maybe he has stepped out for a while, or he has gone on a trip. Or maybe he is asleep, and you have to wake him up!"

decisions.choice: mocked: taunted them with ridicule
decisions.reason: The verb means to deceive or make a fool of someone. Elijah pretends to take Baal seriously in order to show how empty he is.

decisions.choice: for he is a god: said in mockery
decisions.reason: Elijah is not granting that Baal is a god. The words are sarcastic: if he really is a god, he should hear loud enough calling.

decisions.choice: a going aside: he has stepped away, perhaps to relieve himself
alternatives: he has gone aside to relieve himself
decisions.reason: The noun occurs only here. It comes from a verb meaning to move away or withdraw. It may be a polite way of saying that someone has gone aside to relieve himself, as other veiled expressions do (Judges 3:24; 1 Samuel 24:4); if so, Elijah's mockery is coarse. The text does not make this certain, so the words are given in their plain sense.

decisions.choice: musing, traveling, sleeping: mocking stories told of the gods
decisions.reason: Neighboring peoples told stories in which their gods slept, traveled, fought or died and came back to life; the ancient texts of Ugarit tell such things of Baal. Elijah turns this to ridicule. Yahweh, by contrast, "does not slumber or sleep" (Psalm 121:4).

decisions.choice: a going aside (Literal); stepped aside (Balanced); stepped out for a while (Readable)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the plain sense, which leaves open the coarser reading given in the note.

records.source: וַֽיִּקְרְאוּ֙ בְּק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וַיִּתְגֹּֽדְדוּ֙ כְּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔ם בַּחֲרָב֖וֹת וּבָֽרְמָחִ֑ים עַד־שְׁפָךְ־דָּ֖ם עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they called with a voice great and cut themselves according to their custom with swords and with spears until poured out blood on them.
pieces: So they shouted louder and, as was their practice, slashed themselves with swords and spears until the blood flowed over them.

L.28: And they called with a great voice and gashed themselves according to their custom with swords and with spears, until blood poured out over them.

R.28: So they shouted even louder. They cut themselves with swords and spears, as they usually did in their worship, until they were covered with blood.

decisions.choice: gashed themselves: a ritual of mourning and pleading in Canaanite worship
decisions.reason: Cutting the body was a way of mourning and of moving a god to act. Israel was forbidden to do it (Deuteronomy 14:1, where the same verb is used; Leviticus 19:28). The rite fits worship of a god thought to die and rise with the seasons.

decisions.choice: their custom: their regular practice
decisions.reason: The noun usually means a judgment or ruling; here it means what was usual for them, their accustomed rite (compare 2 Kings 17:33).

decisions.choice: spears: light thrusting spears or lances
decisions.reason: The word names a spear or lance (Judges 5:8; Numbers 25:7).

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ כַּעֲבֹ֣ר הַֽצָּהֳרַ֔יִם וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֔וּ עַ֖ד לַעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֑ה וְאֵֽין־ק֥וֹל וְאֵין־עֹנֶ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין קָֽשֶׁב׃
records.gloss: And it was as passed the noon, and they prophesied until the going up of the offering; and there [was] no voice and no one answering and no attention.
pieces: Midday passed, and they went on raving in prophetic frenzy until the time for the evening offering. But there was no sound, no answer, no one taking notice.

L.29: And it was, as noon passed, that they prophesied until the offering up of the offering; but [there was] no voice and no one answering and no attention.

R.29: Noon passed, and they kept on shouting and raving wildly until it was time for the evening sacrifice. But no sound came. No one answered. No one was listening.

decisions.choice: prophesied: raved in an ecstatic frenzy
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to speak as a prophet, but in this form it can describe wild, uncontrolled behavior thought to come from a spirit (1 Samuel 10:5-6; 18:10, of Saul raving in his house). Here it describes the prophets' frenzied cries and actions, not true prophecy.

decisions.choice: the offering up of the offering: the evening sacrifice, in the afternoon
decisions.reason: The offering named here was presented at the end of the day (2 Kings 16:15; Ezra 9:4-5), at the time of the evening lamb (Exodus 29:38-41). The prophets of Baal had called from morning until late afternoon.

decisions.choice: no voice, no one answering, no attention: complete silence
decisions.reason: Verse 26 had "no voice and no one answering"; now a third phrase is added. Baal neither speaks, nor answers, nor even listens.

decisions.choice: prophesied (Literal); raving in prophetic frenzy (Balanced); shouting and raving wildly (Readable); the evening offering
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the usual word; Balanced and Readable say what kind of prophesying this was. Balanced and Readable name the offering by its time of day.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֤הוּ לְכָל־הָעָם֙ גְּשׁ֣וּ אֵלַ֔י וַיִּגְּשׁ֥וּ כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֵלָ֑יו וַיְרַפֵּ֛א אֶת־מִזְבַּ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה הֶהָרֽוּס׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah to all the people, Draw near to me; and drew near all the people to him. And he repaired [the] altar of Yahweh [which was] torn down.
pieces: Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come here to me." When they had all come near, he repaired {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar, which had been torn down.

L.30: And Elijah said to all the people, "Come near to me." And all the people came near to him. And he repaired the altar of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [that was] torn down.

R.30: Then Elijah said to all the people, "Come closer to me." So they all came close to him. Elijah rebuilt {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s altar, which had been torn down.

decisions.choice: repaired: restored, literally "healed"
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual word for healing. Restoring Yahweh's altar is a sign of healing the people's broken worship.

decisions.choice: the altar of Yahweh that was torn down: an old altar on Carmel
decisions.reason: There had been an altar to Yahweh on Carmel. It had been pulled down, perhaps in the attack on Yahweh's worship under Jezebel; Elijah later complains that Israel has torn down Yahweh's altars (19:10, 14).

decisions.choice: come near ... came near: the people are drawn to Elijah's side
decisions.reason: Elijah had come near to the people to challenge them (verse 21); now they come near to him, to watch at close range so no trick is possible.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֵלִיָּ֗הוּ שְׁתֵּ֤ים עֶשְׂרֵה֙ אֲבָנִ֔ים כְּמִסְפַּ֖ר שִׁבְטֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־יַעֲקֹ֑ב אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֥ה שְׁמֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And took Elijah twelve stones according to [the] number of [the] tribes of [the] sons of Jacob, to whom came [the] word of Yahweh, saying, Israel will be your name.
pieces: Elijah took twelve stones, one for each tribe descended from the sons of Jacob, the man to whom the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had come: "Your name will be Israel."

L.31: And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came, saying, "Israel shall be your name."

R.31: He took twelve stones, one for each of the tribes that came from the sons of Jacob. ({{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to Jacob and told him, "Your name will be Israel.")

decisions.choice: Israel shall be your name: God's words to Jacob
decisions.reason: The words echo Genesis 35:10, where God tells Jacob, "Israel shall be your name", and Genesis 32:29, where he first receives the name. All twelve tribes come from the one man God named Israel.

decisions.choice: twelve stones: the whole people of God
decisions.reason: The kingdom had been split, and only ten tribes belonged to Ahab's kingdom (11:31; 12:20). By using twelve stones Elijah declares that Yahweh's people is still one people. Moses set up twelve pillars at Sinai (Exodus 24:4), and Joshua twelve stones at the Jordan (Joshua 4:3-9).

decisions.choice: to whom: to Jacob
decisions.reason: The relative refers to Jacob himself, not to the tribes.

decisions.choice: Readable puts the reminder about Jacob in a separate sentence
decisions.reason: Readable makes the reference to Jacob its own sentence and names him, so it is clear who received the word.

records.source: וַיִּבְנֶ֧ה אֶת־הָאֲבָנִ֛ים מִזְבֵּ֖חַ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיַּ֣עַשׂ תְּעָלָ֗ה כְּבֵית֙ סָאתַ֣יִם זֶ֔רַע סָבִ֖יב לַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃
records.gloss: And he built the stones [into] an altar in [the] name of Yahweh, and he made a trench, like [the] house of two seahs of seed, around the altar.
pieces: He used the stones to build an altar in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and around the altar he dug a trench large enough to hold {{units:about 13 quarts|two seahs}} of seed.

L.32: And he built the stones [into] an altar in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he made a trench, like the house of two seahs of seed, around the altar.

R.32: He used the stones to build an altar for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Around the altar he dug a ditch big enough to hold {{units:about 13 quarts|two seahs}} of seed.

decisions.choice: in the name of Yahweh: for Yahweh and by his authority
decisions.reason: An altar built in Yahweh's name belongs to him and is used to call on him (verse 24; Exodus 20:24).

decisions.choice: like the house of two seahs of seed: the size of the trench
alternatives: enclosing the area of a field sown with two seahs of seed
decisions.reason: A seah was a dry measure, about a third of an ephah. The phrase most likely means a trench that could hold two seahs of grain. It may instead mean that the trench enclosed an area the size of a field sown with two seahs of seed (compare Leviticus 27:16). Either way it was a large trench.

decisions.choice: about 13 quarts (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: A seah is a third of an ephah, so two seahs is about 13 quarts. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit.

decisions.choice: ditch (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for a trench.

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲרֹ֖ךְ אֶת־הָֽעֵצִ֑ים וַיְנַתַּח֙ אֶת־הַפָּ֔ר וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־הָעֵצִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he arranged the wood and cut in pieces the bull and put [it] on the wood.
pieces: He arranged the wood, cut the bull into pieces, and laid it on the wood.

L.33: And he arranged the wood and cut the bull in pieces and put [it] on the wood.

R.33: He stacked the wood on the altar. Then he cut the bull into pieces and laid them on the wood.

decisions.choice: arranged the wood ... laid it on: the usual order for a burnt offering
decisions.reason: Elijah prepares the offering as the law describes for a burnt offering (Leviticus 1:7-9), exactly as he said he would (verse 23).

decisions.choice: verse numbers: many Bibles end this verse later
decisions.reason: In many Bibles this verse also includes Elijah's first order about the water, which in the Hebrew text begins verse 34. See the note there.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִלְא֨וּ אַרְבָּעָ֤ה כַדִּים֙ מַ֔יִם וְיִֽצְק֥וּ עַל־הָעֹלָ֖ה וְעַל־הָעֵצִ֑יםוַיֹּ֤אמֶר שְׁנוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁנ֔וּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר שַׁלֵּ֖שׁוּ וַיְשַׁלֵּֽשׁוּ׃
records.gloss: And he said, Fill four jars [with] water and pour [it] on the burnt offering and on the wood. And he said, Do [it] a second time; and they did [it] a second time. And he said, Do [it] a third time; and they did [it] a third time.
pieces: Then he said, "Fill four jars with water and pour it over the burnt offering and the wood." "Again," he said, and they did it again. "Once more," he said, and they did it a third time.

L.34: And he said, "Fill four jars [with] water and pour [it] on the burnt offering and on the wood." And he said, "Do [it] a second time," and they did [it] a second time. And he said, "Do [it] a third time," and they did [it] a third time.

R.34: Then he said, "Fill four big jars with water. Pour the water over the offering and the wood." Then he said, "Do it again." So they did. Then he said, "Do it a third time." And they did that too.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins verse 34 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text verse 33 ends with the bull laid on the wood, and verse 34 begins with "Fill four jars with water". Many Bibles put that order at the end of verse 33, so the two verses divide at a different place. The words are the same and the following verses are numbered alike; only the break differs.

decisions.choice: water poured three times: no fire could be hidden or easily lit
decisions.reason: Soaking the offering, the wood and the altar rules out any trick and makes the fire harder to kindle. In a time of drought, water was precious; Elijah spends it freely before the God who will send rain.

decisions.choice: jars: large pottery jars for carrying water
decisions.reason: The word names the jars used to draw water and carry it on the shoulder (Genesis 24:14-16).

decisions.choice: Again ... A third time (Balanced)
decisions.reason: Balanced gives Elijah's short commands briefly, as the Hebrew does with one word each.

records.source: וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ הַמַּ֔יִם סָבִ֖יב לַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְגַ֥ם אֶת־הַתְּעָלָ֖ה מִלֵּא־מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And went the water around the altar, and also the trench he filled [with] water.
pieces: The water ran down all around the altar, and he also filled the trench with water.

L.35: And the water went around the altar, and he also filled the trench [with] water.

R.35: The water ran down on every side of the altar. Elijah filled the ditch with water too.

decisions.choice: he also filled the trench: Elijah filled it with more water
decisions.reason: The subject "he" is Elijah. Besides the water that ran down from the altar, he had the trench filled to the brim.

decisions.choice: Elijah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable names Elijah as the subject.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּעֲל֣וֹת הַמִּנְחָ֗ה וַיִּגַּ֞שׁ אֵלִיָּ֣הוּ הַנָּבִיא֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָם֙ יִצְחָ֣ק וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיּ֣וֹם יִוָּדַ֗ע כִּֽי־אַתָּ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַאֲנִ֣י עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וּבִדְבָרְךָ֣ עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And it was at the going up of the offering, and drew near Elijah the prophet and said, Yahweh, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, today let it be known that you [are] God in Israel and I [am] your servant, and by your word I have done all the things these.
pieces: At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet stepped forward and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, today make it known that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God in Israel, that I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and that it is at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word that I have done all this.

L.36: And it was, at the offering up of the offering, that Elijah the prophet came near and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, today let it be known that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] God in Israel, and I [am] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave, and by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I have done all these things.

R.36: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, the prophet Elijah came up to the altar and prayed, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, show everyone today that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are God in Israel. Show them that I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, and that I have done all this because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told me to.

decisions.choice: the offering up of the offering: the evening sacrifice
decisions.reason: See verse 29. Elijah prays at the hour of the regular evening offering, when the prophets of Baal had at last given up.

decisions.choice: God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel: the God of the fathers
decisions.reason: The title recalls Yahweh's name for himself at the burning bush (Exodus 3:6, 15). Elijah says "Israel" rather than "Jacob", pointing back to the new name in verse 31 and to the people gathered before him.

decisions.choice: by your word (the reading the scribes marked)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "by your words"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "by your word". The meaning is the same: Elijah acted on Yahweh's command.

decisions.choice: your servant: Elijah as Yahweh's servant
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a slave, a person who belongs to a master. As Elijah's title it is an honor: he serves Yahweh alone (verse 15).

decisions.choice: your slave (Literal); your servant (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for this word in these books. Elijah's prayer runs on to verse 37.

records.source: עֲנֵ֤נִי יְהוָה֙ עֲנֵ֔נִי וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְאַתָּ֛ה הֲסִבֹּ֥תָ אֶת־לִבָּ֖ם אֲחֹרַנִּֽית׃
records.gloss: Answer me, Yahweh, answer me, and let know the people this that you, Yahweh, [are] the God, and you have turned their heart backward.
pieces: Answer me, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, answer me, so that these people may know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, are God and are turning their hearts back again."

L.37: Answer me, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, answer me, that this people may know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [are] God, and [that] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have turned their heart back."

R.37: Answer me, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! Answer me! Then these people will know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, are the true God, and that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are bringing their hearts back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: you have turned their heart back: you are bringing them back to yourself
alternatives: you turned their hearts away (backward) from you
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn something around, and the adverb means "backward". Most naturally Elijah asks that the people may see Yahweh at work turning their hearts back to him. The words can also mean that Yahweh had let their hearts turn away from him, as a judgment, before now winning them back.

decisions.choice: God: the true God
decisions.reason: With the article, "the God", as in verses 21, 24 and 39.

decisions.choice: answer me, answer me: urgent repetition
decisions.reason: The prophets of Baal cried "Baal, answer us" all day (verse 26). Elijah's short prayer uses the same verb twice.

decisions.choice: back to you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable states the first reading of the note; Balanced keeps the plainer "back again".

records.source: וַתִּפֹּ֣ל אֵשׁ־יְהוָ֗ה וַתֹּ֤אכַל אֶת־הָֽעֹלָה֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣עֵצִ֔ים וְאֶת־הָאֲבָנִ֖ים וְאֶת־הֶעָפָ֑ר וְאֶת־הַמַּ֥יִם אֲשֶׁר־בַּתְּעָלָ֖ה לִחֵֽכָה׃
records.gloss: And fell [the] fire of Yahweh and consumed the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust, and the water which [was] in the trench it licked up.
pieces: Then fire from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fell. It burned up the burnt offering, the wood, the stones and the soil, and licked up the water in the trench.

L.38: And the fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood and the stones and the dust, and it licked up the water that [was] in the trench.

R.38: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sent fire down from the sky. It burned up the offering, the wood, the stones and even the dirt. It dried up all the water in the ditch.

decisions.choice: the fire of Yahweh: fire sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: Fire from Yahweh had consumed offerings before as a sign that he accepted them (Leviticus 9:24; Judges 6:21; 1 Chronicles 21:26). This fire answers the test of verse 24.

decisions.choice: the stones and the dust: even the altar itself and the ground
decisions.reason: The fire consumes more than any ordinary fire could: the stones of the altar and the earth around it. The water is "licked up" like something devoured.

decisions.choice: licked up (Literal, Balanced); dried up (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the result in plain words.

decisions.choice: sent fire down from the sky (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable makes Yahweh the subject and adds where the fire came from, which "fell" implies.

records.source: וַיַּרְא֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ יְהוָה֙ ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים יְהוָ֖ה ה֥וּא הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And saw all the people and fell on their faces and said, Yahweh, he [is] the God; Yahweh, he [is] the God!
pieces: When all the people saw it, they fell face down and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is God! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is God!"

L.39: And all the people saw [it] and fell on their faces and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] God! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] God!"

R.39: When all the people saw this, they bowed down with their faces to the ground. They shouted, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the true God! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the true God!"

decisions.choice: Yahweh, he is God: Israel's confession
decisions.reason: The words answer the question Elijah set in verses 21 and 24. They repeat Moses' words, "Yahweh, he is God; there is no other besides him" (Deuteronomy 4:35, 39). Elijah's own name means "my God is Yahweh".

decisions.choice: fell on their faces: worship and awe
decisions.reason: The people fall to the ground as Israel did when fire came from Yahweh on the first offerings (Leviticus 9:24).

decisions.choice: the LORD is the true God (Readable)
decisions.reason: The pronoun "he" repeats the subject for emphasis. Readable carries the emphasis with "the true God" instead.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ לָהֶ֜ם תִּפְשׂ֣וּ׀אֶת־נְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל אִ֛ישׁ אַל־יִמָּלֵ֥ט מֵהֶ֖ם וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂ֑וּם וַיּוֹרִדֵ֤ם אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־נַ֣חַל קִישׁ֔וֹן וַיִּשְׁחָטֵ֖ם שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah to them, Seize [the] prophets of the Baal; a man not let escape of them. And they seized them, and brought them down Elijah to [the] wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.
pieces: Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal. Do not let one of them get away!" They seized them, and Elijah took them down to the Kishon River and put them to death there.

L.40: And Elijah said to them, "Seize the prophets of Baal; let not a man of them escape!" And they seized them, and Elijah brought them down to the wadi Kishon and slaughtered them there.

R.40: Then Elijah told the people, "Grab the prophets of Baal! Do not let any of them escape!" So the people grabbed them. Elijah led them down to the Kishon River and killed them there.

decisions.choice: the wadi Kishon: the stream below Mount Carmel
decisions.reason: A wadi is a stream bed that may run dry in summer and flood in the rainy season. The Kishon flows west through the Jezreel valley and reaches the sea at the foot of Carmel (Judges 4:7; 5:21).

decisions.choice: the death of the prophets of Baal: the law's sentence on those who lead Israel to other gods
decisions.reason: The law ordered death for a prophet who urged Israel to follow other gods (Deuteronomy 13:2-6; compare 17:2-5). Elijah carries out that sentence on the prophets who led Israel to Baal, and so the account reports the judgment as part of Israel's return to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: put to death
decisions.reason: The verb is often used for slaughtering animals, including sacrifices. It describes a deliberate execution.

decisions.choice: the Kishon River (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Judges 4:7, "wadi" is not a common English word, so Balanced and Readable say "river"; the meaning decision explains that it was a seasonal stream.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ֙ לְאַחְאָ֔ב עֲלֵ֖ה אֱכֹ֣ל וּשְׁתֵ֑ה כִּי־ק֖וֹל הֲמ֥וֹן הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃
records.gloss: And said Elijah to Ahab, Go up, eat and drink, for [the] sound of [the] roar of the rain.
pieces: Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink. There is the sound of a roaring downpour."

L.41: And Elijah said to Ahab, "Go up, eat and drink, for [there is the] sound of the roar of rain."

R.41: Then Elijah said to Ahab, "Go on up and have something to eat and drink. I hear the roar of a heavy rain coming."

decisions.choice: go up: from the Kishon valley back up the mountain
decisions.reason: Elijah had taken the prophets down to the Kishon (verse 40). Ahab is to go back up, perhaps to where his tent was pitched for the gathering.

decisions.choice: the sound of the roar of rain: what the prophet hears before anything can be seen
decisions.reason: The sky is still clear (verses 43-44). Elijah speaks of the rain as already on its way, trusting Yahweh's promise in verse 1.

decisions.choice: I hear (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds who hears the sound.

records.source: וַיַּעֲלֶ֥ה אַחְאָ֖ב לֶאֱכֹ֣ל וְלִשְׁתּ֑וֹת וְאֵ֨לִיָּ֜הוּ עָלָ֨ה אֶל־רֹ֤אשׁ הַכַּרְמֶל֙ וַיִּגְהַ֣ר אַ֔רְצָה וַיָּ֥שֶׂם פָּנָ֖יו בֵּ֥ין בִּרְכָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And went up Ahab to eat and to drink; and Elijah went up to [the] top of the Carmel, and he bent down to the ground and put his face between his knees.
pieces: So Ahab went up to eat and drink, while Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel. He bowed down to the ground and put his face between his knees.

L.42: And Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel, and he bent down to the ground and put his face between his knees.

R.42: So Ahab went up to eat and drink. Elijah, though, climbed to the top of Mount Carmel. There he crouched down on the ground and put his face between his knees.

decisions.choice: Ahab went up ... Elijah went up: two men, two purposes
decisions.reason: The same verb is used for both. The king goes up to feast; the prophet goes up to pray.

decisions.choice: face between his knees: a posture of earnest prayer
decisions.reason: Elijah crouches to the ground with his head bowed low. James 5:18 says he prayed and the sky gave rain.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶֽל־נַעֲר֗וֹ עֲלֵֽה־נָא֙ הַבֵּ֣ט דֶּֽרֶךְ־יָ֔ם וַיַּ֨עַל֙ וַיַּבֵּ֔ט וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵ֣ין מְא֑וּמָה וַיֹּ֕אמֶר שֻׁ֖ב שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he said to his young man, Go up, please, look [toward the] way of [the] sea; and he went up and looked and said, There is not anything. And he said, Go back, seven times.
pieces: He said to his servant, "Go up and look toward the sea." The servant went up and looked, and said, "There is nothing there." Seven times Elijah told him, "Go back."

L.43: And he said to his young man, "Go up, please, look toward the sea." And he went up and looked and said, "[There is] nothing." And he said, "Go back," seven times.

R.43: He told his servant, "Go up and look out toward the sea." The servant went and looked. Then he came back and said, "I do not see anything." Seven times Elijah told him, "Go and look again."

decisions.choice: his young man: his servant
decisions.reason: The word means a young man, and often a servant or attendant (Genesis 22:3; 1 Samuel 9:3).

decisions.choice: the sea: the Mediterranean, to the west
decisions.reason: From the top of Carmel the sea lies to the west and northwest. Rain came to Israel from the sea.

decisions.choice: go back seven times: he was sent again and again, until the seventh time
decisions.reason: The servant went back each time Elijah sent him, and on the seventh time he saw the cloud (verse 44). Seven marks completeness.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ בַּשְּׁבִעִ֔ית וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה־עָ֛ב קְטַנָּ֥ה כְּכַף־אִ֖ישׁ עֹלָ֣ה מִיָּ֑ם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עֲלֵ֨ה אֱמֹ֤ר אֶל־אַחְאָב֙ אֱסֹ֣ר וָרֵ֔ד וְלֹ֥א יַעַצָרְכָ֖ה הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃
records.gloss: And it was at the seventh, and he said, There! a cloud small like [the] palm of a man rising from [the] sea. And he said, Go up, say to Ahab, Harness and go down, and not will stop you the rain.
pieces: The seventh time the servant said, "Look, a cloud as small as a man's hand is rising out of the sea." Elijah said, "Go up and tell Ahab, 'Hitch up your chariot and go down before the rain stops you.'"

L.44: And it was at the seventh [time] that he said, "Look, a cloud, small as a man's palm, rising from the sea!" And he said, "Go up, say to Ahab, 'Harness and go down, so that the rain does not stop you.'"

R.44: The seventh time, the servant said, "I see a little cloud coming up from the sea. It is only about as big as a man's hand." Then Elijah said, "Go and tell Ahab, 'Get your chariot ready and go down the mountain now, or the rain will stop you.'"

decisions.choice: a man's palm: a very small cloud
decisions.reason: The cloud is no bigger than the palm of a hand. From so small a sign Elijah knows the rain is coming.

decisions.choice: harness: harness the horses to the chariot
decisions.reason: The verb means to tie or bind; used alone it means to hitch up the horses to a chariot (Genesis 46:29; 2 Kings 9:21). Verse 45 shows Ahab riding.

decisions.choice: go down, so the rain does not stop you: before the plain floods
decisions.reason: Ahab had to go down from Carmel and cross the Jezreel valley to reach Jezreel (verse 45). Heavy rain could turn the plain to mud and flood the Kishon (Judges 5:21), stopping a chariot.

decisions.choice: Hitch up your chariot (Balanced); Get your chariot ready (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the chariot, which the verb implies.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀עַד־כֹּ֣ה וְעַד־כֹּ֗ה וְהַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ הִֽתְקַדְּרוּ֙ עָבִ֣ים וְר֔וּחַ וַיְהִ֖י גֶּ֣שֶׁם גָּד֑וֹל וַיִּרְכַּ֥ב אַחְאָ֖ב וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ יִזְרְעֶֽאלָה׃
records.gloss: And it was until thus and until thus, and the heavens grew dark [with] clouds and wind, and there was a rain great. And rode Ahab and went to Jezreel.
pieces: Meanwhile, in a very short time, the sky grew black with clouds and wind, and a heavy rain came. Ahab rode off and went to Jezreel.

L.45: And it was, in [the time] until thus and until thus, that the heavens grew dark [with] clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.

R.45: In just a little while, the sky turned black with clouds. The wind blew, and a heavy rain began to fall. Ahab got into his chariot and rode off toward Jezreel.

decisions.choice: until thus and until thus: meanwhile, in a very short time
decisions.reason: The expression means "while this and that was happening" or "in no time at all". The storm builds while Ahab is still getting ready.

decisions.choice: Jezreel: a royal city in the valley east of Carmel
decisions.reason: Ahab had a palace at Jezreel as well as at Samaria (21:1). It lay across the plain from Carmel, a journey of some hours by chariot.

decisions.choice: a great rain: the drought ends
decisions.reason: Yahweh keeps his word of verse 1. The God who answered by fire (verse 38) now answers with rain, the gift Baal was believed to give.

decisions.choice: got into his chariot (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds the chariot, as in verse 44.

records.source: וְיַד־יְהוָ֗ה הָֽיְתָה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ וַיְשַׁנֵּ֖ס מָתְנָ֑יו וַיָּ֨רָץ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אַחְאָ֔ב עַד־בֹּאֲכָ֖ה יִזְרְעֶֽאלָה׃
records.gloss: And [the] hand of Yahweh was on Elijah, and he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab until your coming to Jezreel.
pieces: The hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Elijah. He tucked his robe into his belt and ran in front of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.

L.46: And the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was on Elijah, and he girded up his loins and ran before Ahab until [the] coming to Jezreel.

R.46: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave Elijah special strength. He tied up his long robe so he could run, and he ran ahead of Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel.

decisions.choice: the hand of Yahweh was on Elijah: Yahweh's power came on him
decisions.reason: The "hand" of Yahweh is his power at work in a person, often giving a prophet a message or strength (2 Kings 3:15; Ezekiel 1:3). Here it gives Elijah strength to outrun the king's chariot.

decisions.choice: girded up his loins: tucked his long robe into his belt to run
decisions.reason: Men wore long robes. To run or work they pulled up the lower part and tucked it into the belt at the waist (2 Kings 4:29; 9:1).

decisions.choice: ran before Ahab: like a royal runner going ahead of the king
decisions.reason: Runners went before a king's chariot to clear the way and honor him (1 Samuel 8:11; 2 Samuel 15:1). The prophet who opposed Ahab now runs before him, perhaps as a sign that the king may yet return to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: until your coming to Jezreel: all the way to Jezreel
decisions.reason: The expression "until you come to" is a fixed way of saying "as far as" (Genesis 10:19).

decisions.choice: girded up his loins (Literal); tucked his robe into his belt (Balanced); tied up his long robe so he could run (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom. Balanced and Readable say what Elijah did, and Readable why.

decisions.choice: gave Elijah special strength (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the idiom "the hand of the LORD" in this setting.
